series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: While loading ticks or converting M1 bars, ModePlot is set to PRICE_EXCHANGE (Last/chart last) when any tick/bar has real_volume>0, else PRICE_FOREX (Bid chart). Custom symbol SYMBOL_CHART_MODE and SYMBOL_TRADE_CALC_MODE follow that flag so replay/sim treats exchange vs FX microstructure as two regimes.

why_new_for_mis: Turns presence/absence of traded real_volume into an explicit instrument microstructure regime bit (Bid book vs Last prints) rather than a manual symbol-type setting.
quote: the information that determines whether a bar file belongs to forex (where we use the Bid value as the traded price) or a stock market (where we use Las as the traded price) is precisely the volume.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: Bid-update tick_volume activity when volume_real is zero
mechanism: For PRICE_FOREX bars, each tick with bid>0 increments tick_volume (new bar starts at 1); for PRICE_EXCHANGE, only ticks with volume_real>0 count. Activity is therefore quote-update rate on Bid markets and trade-print rate on Last markets.
data_needed: Tick stream with bid and volume_real; ModePlot; M1 aggregation
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex Bid assets and exchange Last assets; tick→M1 conversion and live CreateBarInReplay
why_new_for_mis: Defines a dual activity sensor: quote-refresh intensity for zero-volume Bid markets versus trade intensity for Last markets—usable as liquidity/activity without assuming prints exist.
quote: When we use the Last plotting mode, in order for the tick volume to be correct, we must start the counter from scratch. But when we use plotting by Bid, we must start the value from one.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: bar-spread floor with randomized excess spread
mechanism: Mount_BID/MountPrice sets ask = bid + tick_size*spread where spread for open/close/extremes is the M1 bar.spread (treated as the minimum observed in that minute for realism), and intermediate ticks use rate.spread + RandomLimit((rate.spread | (imax & 0xF)), 0) so excess widen is bounded by a bitwise mix of bar spread and low bits of tick count.
data_needed: M1 bars with spread field; SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE; digit normalization
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex Bid simulation from M1 bars; also applied when Bid path is reused; 1-minute bars
why_new_for_mis: Treats each M1 bar’s reported spread as a hard liquidity floor and models intra-bar spread widen as a bounded random excess—usable as a per-bar liquidity/cost sensor, not only for synthetic ticks.
quote: If you are running a simulation to obtain a system that resembles what would happen in a real market ... then you will notice that the spread used is the smaller of the values present in the formation of the 1 minute bar.

mechanism: Author states RW pathing is inappropriate when trading volume is low (less than ~500 trades per minute) or when high–low range already exceeds available ticks including open→extreme and extreme→close legs; Bid/Forex sim therefore switches away from prior RW toward bounded RandomLimit(high,low) fills that still hit OHLC.
data_needed: M1 tick_volume, high, low, open, close, tick size; count of ticks available to place
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex Bid assets under simulation; low-liquidity exchange cases flagged for next part; 1-minute bars
why_new_for_mis: Frames sparse tick density relative to price range as a liquidity-regime switch that changes which path generator is valid—directly transferable as a live sparse-vs-dense microstructure flag.
quote: when we are dealing with low trading volume (less than 500 trades per minute), then random walk is completely inappropriate.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: CheckViability path-length vs tick_volume dense/sparse regime
mechanism: CheckViability converts (high−low), max(open→low, open→high), and the longer close→extreme leg into tick steps, inflates each with a safety factor (1.4 then 1.7 via ceil), sums them, and returns true only if that inflated path length < rate.tick_volume—i.e. enough prints to support a non-artificial RW covering the bar.
data_needed: M1 OHLC, tick_volume, tick size; safety-factor constant
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex Bid and stock Last from M1; EURUSD demo files; any 1-minute bar with tick_volume
why_new_for_mis: Gives a concrete dense-vs-sparse microstructure test: required covering path (with safety margin) versus observed tick_volume—usable as a liquidity/activity regime bit independent of the simulator.
quote: The function does exactly this - it calculates the longest possible way to create a 1-minute bar. ... In the end, we make a simple calculation to check whether or not it is possible to use the random walk.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: When structuring a three-phase RandomWalk (open→first extreme, cross to other extreme, then to close), if tick_volume < 1000 the first target is the nearer extreme: b0 = (high−open) < (open−low); if volume ≥ 1000 the first extreme is coin-flipped. Gap step i2 = max(1, (high−low)/tick_size / first_segment_len) allows sparse RW with gaps.
data_needed: M1 OHLC and tick_volume; tick size; segment length fraction min(iMax/3, 0.2*iMax)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD forex Bid and exchange Last M1 bars; compared to real-tick charts in figures
why_new_for_mis: Encodes open-to-high vs open-to-low proximity plus a 1000-tick density threshold as an explicit intra-bar imbalance / effort sensor for which extreme is hit first.
quote: This method, known as the "least effort path", is effective in situations where the number of movements required is less than the total distance to be walked.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
idea_name: tick-count gate structured-walk vs pure Random_Price
mechanism: Simulation uses structured RandomWalk (with gap displacement) only when m_Marks.iMax > 10; at or below 10 ticks in the minute it falls back to Random_Price (uniform RandomLimit between high and low, then force missing extremes). Volume_real is randomly redistributed across ticks only in Last mode.
data_needed: M1 tick_volume (and real_volume for Last); OHLC; ModePlot
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex and stock/futures M1 from attached BOLSA/FOREX/FUTUROS files; 1-minute bars
why_new_for_mis: Uses a hard per-minute tick-count threshold as a liquidity regime switch between structured pathing and unstructured price draws—simple, instrument-agnostic activity sensing.
quote: the system will attempt to perform a random walk with a minimum volume of only 10 trades. For volumes at or below this threshold, pure randomization will be used

idea_name: one-sided Bid-or-Ask false quote moves in real ticks
mechanism: Author notes real tick files contain intervals where only Bid or only Ask changes ("false" movement); sim deliberately omits these one-sided quote updates and always moves Ask locked to Bid+spread to keep balance. The observation itself is a quote-asymmetry event type.
data_needed: Real tick feed with separate bid and ask time series; flags for which side changed
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex real ticks vs Bid-based simulation; tick timeframe
why_new_for_mis: Identifies one-sided Bid/Ask updates as a distinct microstructure event class MIS could count as quote-pressure / asymmetry sensing, even though the article leaves them out of the simulator.
quote: in a real tick file there are times when we actually have some kind of "false" movement. ... such "false" movements occur when variations occur in only one of the prices, either Bid or ASK.
